chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Salih ibn Sahl who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'May I be your sacrifice! From which thing did God, Mighty and Majestic, create the clay of the believer?' So he said: 'From the clay of the Prophets, so it shall never become impure, ever.'

key_terms.الْأَنْبِيَاء: The Prophets — the chain of divinely appointed prophets, whose clay is the most exalted and pure
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِن: The believer — one who has accepted true faith (iman); in the Shia tradition, this implies recognition of the Imam's authority
key_terms.طِينَة: Clay/substance — used metaphysically in Shia theology to denote the primordial spiritual substance from which a soul was created, determining its innate spiritual disposition

ai.seo_question: From what was the believer's clay created according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Salih ibn Sahl asked Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about the ontological origin of the believer's 'clay' (tinah) — the spiritual substance from which humans are created. The Imam revealed that the believer's clay was created from the same substance as the Prophets, which is why it retains an inherent purity and can never become permanently defiled. This cosmological teaching reflects the Shia doctrine that true believers share a spiritual lineage with the Prophets, giving them an innate capacity for purity and righteousness.
